Just weeks before the Administration moved to block the bridge, Matthew Moroun – whose family owns the competing Ambassador Bridge – gave $1 million to the President’s super PAC. At a minimum, the timing raises serious questions. Friend, when MAGA dark money floods our system, decisions stop being about what’s best for working families – and start being about who can write the biggest check. And in a swing district like ours, we know exactly what that means: more outside money flooding in to try and buy this seat. In fact, it’s already happening – we’ve faced more than $1 million in dark-money spending trying to lie about me and buy this seat. In order to push back – and keep fighting for working families here in mid-Michigan – it’s going to take real grassroots support. Can you chip in $3 now? Here's a good link to donate: = Thank you, Kristen P.S. I’ve attached my original message below. Please give it a read if you haven’t already! \------ Forwarded Message ------ From: Kristen McDonald Rivet Date: Feb 18, 2026, 4:00 PM Subject: Another day, and another inexplicable move by this White House Friend, Another day, and another inexplicable move by this White House that will wreak havoc on working families in Michigan. This time, President Trump is threatening new tariffs on Canada and trying to block the Gordie Howe International Bridge from opening – a decade-in-the-making, bipartisan project, fueled by union labor, that will be a game changer in the supply chain between the US and Canada – which means more jobs and lower costs. When the President picks a fight like this, it created chaos for our manufacturers and small businesses and jacks up the price of everyday goods. And when our economy takes a hit because of this, it’s Michigan workers and families that pay the price. Meanwhile, my opponent says he supports President Trump's tariffs, calling this chaotic policy “the new normal”. He won’t defend the bridge. He won’t stand up to Trump – even when Michigan jobs are on the line. We deserve better than that, friend. In Congress, I’ve been fighting for working families – working to lower everyday costs, expand access to health care, and make sure mid-Michigan families can count on good-paying jobs and a stable economy. name: Ruben Gallego
subject: I won’t be at the State of the Union tonight
disclaimer_text: Paid For By Gallego for Arizona
body:
I never expected that I’d turn down that kind of an opportunity. But that’s what I’m doing this year.
#

Peter, it's Ruben.
I grew up poor. I slept on the floor of our apartment because that’s all we could afford.
I never expected I’d be invited to the State of the Union someday. That would’ve been unbelievable.
And honestly, I never expected that I’d turn down that kind of an opportunity. But that’s what I’m doing this year.
I’m not going to sit there and clap on cue for a guy who is tearing our country apart. When people can’t afford groceries, when he’s trying to start a war with Iran, when Trump’s goons are beating and killing Americans on our own streets — why the hell would I waste my time with that?
Look, no judgment to any of my colleagues that will be there tonight. But for me, no. There’s better things all of us can be doing than listen to that 79 year old wannabe king pat himself on the back.
Maybe it’s the Marine in me, but I’d rather fight.
I am going to do everything I can to make sure Trump is staring down two Democratic majorities at the State of the Union next year.

# [](https://act.sarahmcbride.com/go/1269?t=1&akid=2867%2E21716%2EBcYP24)
Tonight, Donald Trump is going to attempt to tell the American people that the state of our union is strong. But despite what he wants us to believe, the reality for working families is that costs are higher, rights are under attack, and too many people are struggling to make ends meet.
I’ve made the decision to attend his speech because I don’t want him to have the pleasure of speaking to a room full of sycophants. If Democrats don’t show up, Republicans will fill our seats, and Americans will see a chamber full of applause for his failed presidency.
We can’t let that happen — which is why I won’t give up my seat. And as my guest, I’ll be bringing a Delawarean who is standing up every day for our values and our Constitution: Delaware’s Attorney General Kathy Jennings.
While I’m fighting in Congress, Attorney General Jennings is on the front lines fighting in the courts. From fighting Trump’s illegal tariffs that are raising costs to defending health care and food assistance, she’s protecting Delaware consumers, securing federal funding owed to our state, and holding the powerful accountable.
Together, we’re going to keep standing up for Delaware families and pushing back against Trump’s chaos. But I need you with me, too.

Dear , Come join the campaign at the American Croatian Citizens "Cro" Club in Donora on Sunday, March 1 from 2 to 5 for our volunteer appreciation and petition event. It's a great opportunity to meet volunteers from all around the district and find out which county has the best duck pin bowlers. There are six duck pin lanes and six counties in PA-14. I like sharing the Cro Club with my friends because it's a place my mom occasionally took me and my brother when we were young. One grandfather used to bowl in a league there and my other grandfather probably helped lay the brick exterior. To me, it's an iconic blast from the district's past. So come have fun, either by bowling or laughing at your old and new friends who are bowling. For those unfamiliar with duck pin bowling, the ball and pins are smaller. Local kids set the pins manually. It looks really easy, but it's not. Leave your high heels at home, Wear any non-marking shoe. Let's see which county wins the bowling trophy I've repurposed. I'm feeling a growing energy throughout the district. Having fun from time to time is essential for maintaining our mental health and continuing our momentum as we build the community that will win this campaign. In Appreciation, Alan Bradstock

clean_body: | | Dear , Come join the campaign at the American Croatian Citizens "Cro" Club in Donora on Sunday, March 1 from 2 to 5 for our volunteer appreciation and petition event. It's a great opportunity to meet volunteers from all around the district and find out which county has the best duck pin bowlers. There are six duck pin lanes and six counties in PA-14. I like sharing the Cro Club with my friends because it's a place my mom occasionally took me and my brother when we were young. One grandfather used to bowl in a league there and my other grandfather probably helped lay the brick exterior. To me, it's an iconic blast from the district's past. So come have fun, either by bowling or laughing at your old and new friends who are bowling. For those unfamiliar with duck pin bowling, the ball and pins are smaller. Local kids set the pins manually. It looks really easy, but it's not. Leave your high heels at home, Wear any non-marking shoe. Let's see which county wins the bowling trophy I've repurposed. I'm feeling a growing energy throughout the district. Having fun from time to time is essential for maintaining our mental health and continuing our momentum as we build the community that will win this campaign. In Appreciation, Alan Bradstock | ~~ "Facebook" "Instagram" mailto:info@bradstockforcongress.com "Email" "YouTube" ~ "Bluesky" "X" Bradstock for Congress P.O. subject: Everything is on the line
body:
Join Powered by People today
#
I was walking from the parking lot at the University of North Texas over to where our volunteers were setting up our canvassing program, when Kennedy came up to me and just opened up, nearly in tears, about how bad things have become and how hard it is for her to see us getting through it all.
Strange how it works, but I was feeling the same way that morning. Just weighed down by everything I'd read in the news and all the work that I know lies ahead, but somehow her opening up to me turned me back around to where I needed to be. And I hope my talking to her did the same.
And then, for the next five hours, we went out there and met every student we could, checking their registration, listening to what's on their mind, trying to share our hope and optimism rooted in the work that we're doing, and then making a commitment to stay in touch for the next nine months to ensure that we all vote when it really counts.
I heard uplifting and amazing stories, like Jonah, who'd recently moved from Kentucky and was organizing his fellow students at UNT. I heard tough ones, like Ashley who told me her dad, who's lived in North Texas for the last 33 years, had recently been picked up by ICE and was in the process of being deported to Mexico, a country he hasn't been to since he was a kid. She's studying construction management, is focused on her career, on making the most of the opportunity her dad is giving her, and is encouraging others to get registered and vote so that we can have an immigration system that actually works, uniting families instead of separating them.
By the end of the day we'd registered and added hundreds of students to our network. One day. One campus. But it all adds up.
We do it because it works.
In 2024, young people turned out at a rate of 37%. In our program, it was over 79%. That’s not an accident. That’s organizing.
Even if you aren’t in Texas, you can still be part of this important work. [**Whether you can volunteer, help register voters, show up at events, or simply stay connected and help spread the word, there is a role for you in this work — and we need you.**](https://act.leftnet.org/go/22310?source=em20260224-1511&t=1&akid=1511%2E2118727%2Ery2qIH)
**[ADD YOUR NAME ››](https://act.leftnet.org/go/22310?source=em20260224-1511&t=2&akid=1511%2E2118727%2Ery2qIH)**
Remember, action is the antidote to despair, and it is the key to victory.
—Beto

**LeftNet is an online political network fighting for progressive causes and candidates focused on social, racial, economic, and environmental justice.**

body:
About the Supreme Court’s recent tariff decision

| | | [ ](https://act.elizabethwarren.com/go/216?t=3&akid=2793%2E4032634%2EaLhXVC)
---
Donald Trump illegally stole your money — and you are entitled to get it back. The Supreme Court recently ruled that the chaotic tariffs he put in place last year — the tariffs that he dangled in front of other countries to make them bend the knee, made the prices of goods skyrocket, and enabled large corporations to increase prices for consumers to cover the costs — were illegal. Yes: The Supreme Court actually stepped up and actually applied the law. Now, that means we’ve got to work out a way to get the $160 billion in revenue that the federal government got from these tariffs back into the hands of the people it was taken from. **As a reminder, families have paid more than $1,700 each on tariff costs.** 90% of the costs of these tariffs were borne by American families and businesses. But how did the Trump administration respond? Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent, who is in charge of figuring this out, smirked when asked about what’s going to happen to this money and said, “'I got a feeling the American people aren’t going to see it.” What, does he think if the government can’t keep this money that it should just go to a handful of giant corporations? This would give corporations two wins: First when they passed those tariff costs along to consumers, and then again through a refund back to the corporations. **I got a feeling the American people want their money back. And I’m going to bang every drum and shake every table I can find to ensure this money gets refunded to American families and small businesses — not giant corporations.** [**Add your name to keep up the pressure: It's time for American families to get their money back from the government’s illegal tariffs, and it's up to the Trump administration to make that happen.**](https://act.elizabethwarren.com/signup/ew-em-tariff/?source=EMZ29V_TAR_E_20260224_V1S1&t=8&akid=2793%2E4032634%2EaLhXVC) | [**ADD YOUR NAME**](https://act.elizabethwarren.com/signup/ew-em-tariff/?source=EMZ29V_TAR_E_20260224_V1S1&t=9&akid=2793%2E4032634%2EaLhXVC)
---
It’s not that hard: When somebody takes money from you illegally, that's called stealing in the United States. The American people are entitled to the money that was stolen from them, plain and simple.
I’m going to keep up the fight on this.
Thanks for being a part of this,
Elizabeth

I’m preparing to deliver the Democratic response to Donald Trump’s first State of the Union address of his second term tonight – **_and I wanted to reach out to you directly, Derek._**

Team, Tonight, Donald Trump will stand before Congress and the nation to deliver the State of the Union. It will be a speech full of lies. A lot of Democrats are choosing to skip it. I’m not. If you’re going to fight authoritarianism, you don’t do it from the parking lot. You step into the arena. **You defend democracy in the room where it’s being pushed to its limits. ** I believe in confronting Trump wherever he spews his lies and wherever he thinks that he is strongest, whether on Fox News or tonight in the House Chamber. Because that’s what fighters do — and I’m not going alone. Tonight, I’m bringing Marcelo, an incredible young man from Milford, MA, who has lived in the US since he was six years old. He was detained by ICE despite having no criminal history and denied a bed or even a shower for nearly a week before eventually being released. This is the state of Trump’s America: unsafe and unfree. body:

In one week, Texas decides the future of our race — and right now, a Super
PAC is trying to buy this out from under us.

[ https://act.angelaalsobrooks.com/go/40394?t=1015&amount=30&akid=3474%2E52803%2EXvMddS ]I’m asking you directly: will you split a donation between my campaign
and Senator Angela Alsobrooks to help us fund our final voter outreach
push before Election Day?

[ https://act.angelaalsobrooks.com/go/40394?t=1016&amount=10&akid=3474%2E52803%2EXvMddS ]Chip in $10 [ https://act.angelaalsobrooks.com/go/40394?t=1017&amount=30&akid=3474%2E52803%2EXvMddS ]Chip in $30
[ https://act.angelaalsobrooks.com/go/40394?t=1018&amount=50&akid=3474%2E52803%2EXvMddS ]Chip in $50 [ https://act.angelaalsobrooks.com/go/40394?t=1019&amount=100&akid=3474%2E52803%2EXvMddS ]Chip in $100

We are in the last stretch. Early voting is wrapping up. Ballots are being
cast. And outside billionaires are dumping massive money into negative ads
to drown out our message.

They don’t want Texans hearing about accountability, transparency, or a
campaign powered by people instead of powerful interests.

So they’re trying to overwhelm us in the final days.

Here’s the truth: whether we win or lose will come down to what we do
right now.

* We need to scale up digital ads.
* We need to fund text and phone outreach.
* We need to put clipboards in volunteers’ hands and get them knocking
doors.
* We need to make sure every single Texan hears our message before it’s
too late.

This is the final push. There is no “later” and I know you don’t want to
wake up next Wednesday wishing you could have done more.

[ https://act.angelaalsobrooks.com/go/40394?t=1007&amount=30&akid=3474%2E52803%2EXvMddS ]If you believe in this movement — if you believe Texas deserves bold,
accountable leadership — please split a donation between my campaign and
Senator Alsobrooks today to help us fund our voter mobilization efforts in
these last seven days.

We’ve got 7 days to win. Let’s do this.

— Jasmine Crockett

disclaimer_text: Paid for by Friends of Francesca Hong
body:
Support our grassroots campaign
# [](https://francescahong.com?refcode=em20260224-2550)
Peter,
This morning, I put on my trusty gray parka and put out a [challenge](https://act.francescahong.com/go/5057?t=1&akid=2550%2E105371%2ECfvDGN) on social media.
Channeling my inner (and outer!) Bernie Sanders, I asked people to donate $2 to this campaign. That’s it, just $2.
[](https://act.francescahong.com/go/1?c0=em_ms_fh_20260224.loGgh8&refcode=em20260224-2550&t=2&akid=2550%2E105371%2ECfvDGN)
We don’t have big-money donors. But we do have the most popular support in the entire race – over 7,400 individual donations. That’s more than the next two candidates combined. If donations were votes, we'd be winning by a landslide.
This campaign is powered by people like you. When we all work together, the many can beat the money.
To paraphrase JFK: We choose to run a grassroots campaign not because it’s easy, but because it is hard. And because it’s democratic.
Here's what your $2 goes toward:
* Deploying 2000+ volunteers to knock doors in every corner of the state
* Printing yard signs, flyers, and mailers to spread our message far and wide
* Fueling our statewide campus tour so we can keep showing up for young voters who are fired up and ready to organize
* Getting Fran on the road to meet voters face-to-face
* Building the digital infrastructure to reach voters online, tell our story, and fight back against big-money opposition

If every person on this email list chips in, the impact will be huge.
Or as Bernie would say, YUGE.
**[Donate $2 today (or $20, or $200!)](https://act.francescahong.com/go/1?c0=em_ms_fh_20260224.loGgh8&refcode=em20260224-2550&t=3&akid=2550%2E105371%2ECfvDGN)**

With gratitude,
— Fran
**[P.S. Monthly recurring donations are the best way to support our campaign. Even $2 a month helps!](https://act.francescahong.com/go/1?c0=em_ms_fh_20260224.loGgh8&refcode=em20260224-2550&t=23&akid=2550%2E105371%2ECfvDGN)**

_**By David Shuster**_
In government and governance, symbols matter - not because politicians are particularly sentimental, but because the public must be able to trust that someone in leadership is capable of behaving like an adult. In the Trump administration, the latest juvenile embarrassment has been delivered by FBI Director Kash Patel.
This past weekend, Patel decided that his highest and best use, while abroad on official business, was to place himself at the center of a locker room reeking of sweat, triumph and beer foam and celebrate like a college sophomore who just discovered malt liquor.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/0491235a-d3da-41c1-8249-72c300fbcfc9?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|

[Upgrade to paid](https://substack.com/redirect/2/eyJlIjoiaHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuYmx1ZWFtcC5jby9zdWJzY3JpYmU_.3e3QyWiX-6NZwmhHaAWYVytj78QDgKe7cwvy3JiAllI?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget&utm_content=188952792)
* * *
The occasion was the gold-medal Olympic victory of the U.S. men's hockey team. It is a wonderful and impressive accomplishment that required absolutely no assistance from America's chief federal law enforcement agent. Yet there was Patel, draped in borrowed glory, clutching a bottle as though Prohibition had just been repealed again, grinning into cameras in a smarmy manner that suggested the burden of national security had been replaced by the weight of fermentation.
At first glance, this might seem like a trivial breach of decorum -- a powerful official caught enjoying a national sports victory. But the optics and implications go deeper. The FBI director is not a drum major, nor a mascot, nor the fraternity president who bangs the keg to ensure equal distribution. The FBI director is, at least in theory, the sober guardian of the nation's laws -- a man entrusted with counterintelligence, counterterrorism, the challenges of organized crime, and the obligation to help release ALL of the Epstein files. The FBI Director should embody seriousness and stability. The position does not include "assistant equipment manager, post-victory lager division."
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/0491235a-d3da-41c1-8249-72c300fbcfc9?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---

* * *
Of course, given the modern Trump appetite for spectacle and the way his narcissism has infected countless Americans, there are those in MAGA world who find Patel's antics charming. "He's just being one of the guys," they insist, as though our nation's principal law enforcement officer was nominated and confirmed to take over a boisterous locker room. American voters have always had a weakness for officials who appear to be enjoying themselves. It reassures some of us that governance is not too grave a matter.
But the problem here is not merely aesthetic. It is also ethical.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/0491235a-d3da-41c1-8249-72c300fbcfc9?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Federal officials, unlike carnival freaks and late-night sports hosts, are constrained by rules -- among them the charmingly unambiguous 5 C.F.R. § 2635, governing standards of ethical conduct. The federal regulation forbids the misuse of official position, including the use of one's title, authority, or access for private gain or for the appearance of special privilege. It exists because, from time to time, officials are tempted to treat their office as a backstage pass.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/0491235a-d3da-41c1-8249-72c300fbcfc9?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
[Leave a comment](https://substack.com/app-link/post?publication_id=3722532&post_id=188952792&utm_source=substack&utm_medium=email&isFreemail=true&comments=true&token=eyJ1c2VyX2lkIjo5MDUwMTE5MiwicG9zdF9pZCI6MTg4OTUyNzkyLCJpYXQiOjE3NzE5NzgzNTgsImV4cCI6MTc3NDU3MDM1OCwiaXNzIjoicHViLTM3MjI1MzIiLCJzdWIiOiJwb3N0LXJlYWN0aW9uIn0.kP75oWZXGVatCDjORYp3_JSbfxUxXlVbd62b_Z-FxCA&r=1hvr60&utm_campaign=email-half-magic-comments&action=post-comment)
* * *
You don't have to be a graduate of even a top tier law school to ask a simple question: would the average federal employee, traveling abroad on official business, be granted access to a gold-medal locker room celebration for the purpose of drinking alcohol and wearing a medal? Or is such revelry reserved for those who can flash a government title that opens doors not ordinarily open?
When a federal office becomes a key to festivities unavailable to the common taxpayer or government agent, the line between public duty and personal indulgence begins to wobble. And wobble it did with Patel, visibly, effervescently, and with countless classless "F*ck yeah" bombs.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/0491235a-d3da-41c1-8249-72c300fbcfc9?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
The Trump administration insists that Patel will reimburse the government for his personal expenses, that he was in Italy on legitimate bureau business, that the beer was but a modest salute to American excellence. All of that may be technically correct, and at the same time, spiritually absurd. Ethics rules are not accounting devices; they are guardrails against the slow creep of entitlement. They are meant to prevent officials from confusing the applause given to athletes with the applause Patel, Trump, and others in this administration believe are due to themselves.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/0491235a-d3da-41c1-8249-72c300fbcfc9?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---

* * *
There is also the small matter of dignity. The FBI, for all its bureaucratic sins and historic misadventures, rests upon a clear image: dark suits, clipped briefings, unsmiling seriousness. It is difficult to reconcile that solemnity with the photographs and videos of the FBI director grinning beneath a rain of lager, as though auditioning for a commercial titled "Federal Bureau of Libations."
A nation is judged not only by its victories but by the behavior of its leaders and stewards. The U.S. hockey players earned their gold medal through skill, grit, broken teeth, and exceptional on-ice teamwork.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/0491235a-d3da-41c1-8249-72c300fbcfc9?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
[Leave a comment](https://substack.com/app-link/post?publication_id=3722532&post_id=188952792&utm_source=substack&utm_medium=email&isFreemail=true&comments=true&token=eyJ1c2VyX2lkIjo5MDUwMTE5MiwicG9zdF9pZCI6MTg4OTUyNzkyLCJpYXQiOjE3NzE5NzgzNTgsImV4cCI6MTc3NDU3MDM1OCwiaXNzIjoicHViLTM3MjI1MzIiLCJzdWIiOiJwb3N0LXJlYWN0aW9uIn0.kP75oWZXGVatCDjORYp3_JSbfxUxXlVbd62b_Z-FxCA&r=1hvr60&utm_campaign=email-half-magic-comments&action=post-comment)
* * *
Patel earned his position through politics and appointment. And with that comes an obligation for the FBI Director to comport himself in a manner respecting and reflecting the gravity of federal power. The obligation does not dissolve at the sight of championship athletes swigging victory beers and champagne.
Indeed, moments of celebration demand more government leadership restraint, not less. When the public mood is buoyant, the temptation to blur lines grows irresistible. That is precisely when officials must remember that their office is not their personality. It is not their social life. It is not a souvenir to be worn for photographs amid beer spray.
What remains, after the foam settles, is not a charming anecdote but a diminished office. The gold medals will sit in the players' trophy cases, well deserved. The images of the FBI director carousing in their wake will sit elsewhere, especially in the minds of citizens who expect the chief law enforcement officer to project professionalism and maturity.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/0491235a-d3da-41c1-8249-72c300fbcfc9?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Kash Patel behaved like a rowdy, self absorbed teenager living out a sports and alcohol drenched fantasy experience.
Patel didn't deserve to be part of the U.S. locker room celebration. And he took what might have been an inspiring, bipartisan national story about a remarkable U.S. hockey triumph over Canada and diminished it.
The U.S. hockey team earned their gold medals.
FBI Director Kash Patel has earned nothing but contempt.

Hey Peter, it’s Martin Sheen.
You may know me from my roles as an actor — _including a former fictional president_ — but tonight I’m reaching out as an American concerned about the direction our nation is heading.
My character in the West Wing famously said, “I’m the President of the United States, not the president of the people who agree with me.”
_And I think that’s a lesson Donald Trump needs to learn._
As he dismantles checks on his power and purges the government of dissenters, Americans are becoming more and more afraid to speak up and use their constitutionally protected rights to fight back against this administration.
**It’s downright scary and un-American.** The health of our democracy relies on spirited debate and freedom of speech, and we’re seeing this tradition slowly disappear.
In the midst of this chaos, one thing has become clear: We need leaders to reject this turn towards authoritarianism and stand up against Trump.
And right now — as Republicans maintain their hold on Congress and the White House — the only way we can stop the descent to one-man rule is to win in the midterms.
And no one is facing a tougher race than Jon Ossoff in Georgia this year.
Jon is the only Democratic Senator up for reelection in a state Donald Trump won in 2024 and is the GOP’s top target for defeat. He’s a champion for the people of Georgia and a watchdog for corruption.
**He’s exactly the kind of leader we need at a time like this.**
[**That’s why I’m asking you to join me in supporting Jon Ossoff’s reelection campaign today. subject: They bend the rules. We build power.
body:

| | | | | | Friends, I want to make sure you heard what happened this weekend.

**At the California Democratic Party convention, party elites bent their own rules to help my opponent Doris Matsui secure the party’s endorsement in our race.

** Nancy Pelosi interrupted our regional caucus – which is against convention rules – to advocate on Matsui’s behalf.

[**If you're as angry about this as I am, rush in $5, $35, or even $100 to show them we’re done with the status quo.**
](https://maiforus.us3.list-manage.com/track/click?u=fe5f60ccb8fb671f0c1857dc9&id=ac05342d39&e=dd5af5b7b1)

| | Voters are demanding new leadership. Democratic approval ratings are at record lows. People are asking for courage and urgency. And the response from party insiders? Close ranks and protect the status quo.

**That’s their choice.**_**Ours is different.

**_ I didn’t get into this race for a title or an endorsement. I got in because families in California are struggling -- and at a moment when healthcare is being cut, immigrant families are being targeted, and corporate power runs Washington, we deserve leadership accountable to us.

There are fewer than 100 days until the primary election. And the strongest response we can make right now is a wave of grassroots support showing that our district wants new leadership -- not politics-as-usual protected by insiders.

[**If you’re with us, chip in $5, $35, or whatever you can afford and help us prove it before the week is out.**](https://maiforus.us3.list-manage.com/track/click?u=fe5f60ccb8fb671f0c1857dc9&id=ca2d784a69&e=dd5af5b7b1)**

**With heart and hustle,

Mai
